title: Tech sergeant warns Borland never to speak of the triangle again

tellings.quote: He, my tech sergeant, was the one that was like, "Dylan, don't talk about this ever again. You have no idea what you got yourself into."
My my old tech sergeant who I worked with who was a load master, he clearly knew something.
tellings.difference: Identifies the tech sergeant as a loadmaster who clearly knew something.
tellings.link_reason: Both are Borland's tech sergeant warning him not to talk about what he saw.

as_told.title: Loadmaster tech sergeant warned him not to talk

plain: In 2012 at Langley Air Force Base in Virginia, a tech sergeant, a mid-level Air Force rank, warned a young airman never to mention a triangle-shaped object again, telling him, "Dylan, don't talk about this ever again. You have no idea what you got yourself into." The airman, Dylan Borland, tells this himself as the person who got the warning. He describes the sergeant as a loadmaster, the crew member who handles cargo on aircraft, who "clearly knew something," which would suggest the sighting was already known and kept quiet.
